statement: Software is too important to be unreliable or insecure. It underpins our digital world and increasingly controls physical systems. Yet software is increasingly being created and changed faster than people can review it, accelerated by AI-powered development. My research pursues two complementary goals: building intelligent tools that can automatically audit software, find and repair bugs and vulnerabilities, and establishing the methods needed to assure that these tools and the broader AI-enabled systems are reliable and secure.

areas.title: AI for Software Engineering
areas.description: Software development is moving beyond what human review alone can keep pace with. We develop AI-enabled methods that audit code and software artifacts, identify defects and vulnerabilities, trace them to their causes, generate repairs, and validate that proposed fixes are correct. Our goal is to turn AI into a dependable engineering partner that helps developers build and maintain reliable, secure software at scale.

areas.title: Assurance for AI-Enabled Software
areas.description: AI is increasingly used both to create software and as a core component of software systems, from coding assistants to autonomous agents. Failures and vulnerabilities in these systems can propagate into generated code, automated decisions, and real-world actions. We develop rigorous evaluations, realistic benchmarks, and practical defences to understand these risks and improve the reliability and security of AI-assisted development and AI-powered software.

projects.title: PatchGuru
projects.description: Infers patch oracles from the natural language artifacts of a pull request, enabling automated patch validation without hand-written specifications.

projects.title: FormalBench
projects.description: Benchmark and evaluation framework for assessing whether language models can infer formal specifications and reason about program semantics.

projects.title: FLAMES
projects.description: Semantic-guided patch generation that cuts the GPU memory needed for LLM-based program repair while holding repair quality on standard benchmarks.

projects.title: VulGuard
projects.description: Unified tool for training and evaluating just-in-time vulnerability prediction models under realistic data settings.
